candidate_test_answers.answer: I would use a stack. Push opening brackets. For a closing bracket, the stack must be non-empty and its top must be the matching opening bracket; otherwise return false. At the end the stack must be empty. This is O(n) time and O(n) space. Empty input and mismatched or early closing brackets are handled.

I can repeatedly remove valid pairs like (), {}, and [] from the string until no more replacements are possible. If the result is empty it is valid. This is correct, but repeated replacements can make it slower than a stack.

I would use a stack, push opening brackets, and pop when the matching closing bracket appears. The algorithm is correct. I believe the time is O(n^2) because every bracket may require checking the stack, and space is O(n).

I would use a stack to match opening and closing brackets. Push openings and pop when a closing bracket appears. The complexity is O(n) time and O(n) space. I would not specifically handle an empty string or a closing bracket appearing when the stack is empty.
I would push every bracket into a stack and then compare the brackets after reading the string. I am not sure how to handle different bracket types or an unmatched closing bracket.
